summary: Preinstall script downloads Bun runtime and executes an obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is hex-identifier obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style `_0x...` names, per-function string-lookup maps hiding literals such as `bun`, `bun.exe`, `--version`, `Alpine`, `ldd`, and the download URL). At install time it downloads the Bun runtime archive from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/, extracts and chmods it executable, then invokes the Bun binary against a sibling file `math_init.js` (falling back to any `bun` already on PATH). math_init.js is a 727KB Bun-compiled bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header) using a shuffled string-array rotator and a large opaque constant table — its contents are not readable statically and it is executed under a runtime that Node-based scanners typically do not analyze. The package's declared purpose is an ESLint TypeScript/React configuration, which has no need for an alternate JS runtime, a 727KB compiled binary bundle, or an obfuscated install-time bootstrap. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: pulling in a second JS runtime specifically to execute an opaque payload on `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
